page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 38 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 219.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 54.69 GB per core. It includes 262 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the M8-4ms exhibits low compute and memory throughput relative to other server classes. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1035.08 and multi-core score of 2724.76 fall into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 151.25 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 17.71 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both placing in the bottom 10%. Database and key-value operations, such as Redis SET, achieve 2.63 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is measured at 3.0 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the M8-4ms is its extreme imbalance between massive memory capacity and limited processing power. While the qualitative cost efficiency is low for compute-heavy workloads due to weak CPU and memory bandwidth performance, the instance provides high resource density for memory-bound tasks that do not require intensive CPU cycles. This configuration is suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM footprints but minimal parallel processing.
description: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. It is configured with an exceptionally high memory capacity of 219.0 GB (54.69 GB per core) and 262 GB of local storage. Benchmark data reveals significant performance tradeoffs, with both single-core and multi-core CPU metrics placing in the lower percentiles, alongside weak memory bandwidth and database operation speeds. This server is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require massive RAM capacity but have low computational demands, such as large-scale caching, in-memory databases, and legacy enterprise applications.
